news.headline: PPL discovers gas & condensate at Dolphin X-1 well, Sirani Exploration License, Sindh
news.summary: Pakistan Petroleum Limited (PSX: PPL), operator of the Sirani Exploration License (75% working interest, with GHPL holding 25%), disclosed to PSX on Aug 17, 2026 a gas/condensate discovery at exploration well Dolphin X-1 in District Sujawal, Sindh. Well spudded Apr 17, 2026, drilled to 3,850m to test the Chiltan Formation. Post-acid testing: gas flowing at 0.942 mmscfd with heating value ~1,000 Btu/scf. Pre-acid testing: condensate at an initial rate of 94 bbl/day, declining to 46 bbl/day within 24 hours. Business Recorder headline framed it as a 'major exploration win' that 'opened a new exploration frontier across onshore marshy area and its possible extensions into shallow offshore'; however the disclosed flow rate (0.942 mmscfd) is modest relative to PPL's scale. Logged as impact 3 (notable exploration/discovery news) given the disclosed figures do not yet rise to a confirmed material production/reserve addition.

news.headline: Federal Constitutional Court allows tax credit adjustment against super tax
news.summary: Pakistan's Federal Constitutional Court ruled that tax credits granted under Section 168 of the Income Tax Ordinance can be legally adjusted against super tax liability, setting aside a prior Islamabad High Court decision that had denied this to private mobile operator Zong (not a PSX-listed universe ticker) in its dispute with the FBR. Six-page judgment authored by Justice Aamer Farooq holds the tax credit is a 'separate and established legal right' and that fiscal law should be interpreted to facilitate taxpayers. Ruling sets a precedent applicable to corporate taxpayers broadly (banks and other large corporates subject to super tax), potentially reducing effective super-tax cash outflow for eligible taxpayers with unadjusted tax credits. Logged as impact 4 (material regulatory/judicial action with broad corporate-tax implications) per desk news-impact criteria (Rule 10); escalation flagged.
